label: Spacecraft
description: Real rockets, capsules, landers, rovers, satellites, and stations alongside science-fiction spacecraft.
notes: Real space vehicles and exploration hardware belong here alongside distinct science-fiction spacecraft forms. vehicle.aircraft owns craft used primarily for atmospheric flight; vehicle.watercraft owns seagoing freighters. Values are bare generic type names, without mission names, manufacturers, or franchise references. Real hardware has no global tags, including historic equipment; every fictional entry is tagged scifi, and the look describes a recognizable visual convention.

values.look: A tall cylindrical launch vehicle with a pointed payload fairing, stacked stages, and clustered engine bells.
A winged orbital vehicle has a blunt nose, delta wings, a tall tail fin, and three large rear engines.
A squat foil-covered landing module stands on four splayed legs beneath an angular crew cabin.
A compact blunt cone with a broad heat-shield base, small windows, and a narrow docking end.
Connected cylindrical modules and trusswork spread between large rectangular solar-panel arrays.
A six-wheeled robotic explorer has a boxy instrument deck, jointed suspension, and a camera mast.
A boxy orbital satellite has broad flat solar arrays and projecting dish antennas.
A large cylindrical optical instrument has an open front aperture and solar panels extending from its sides.
A robotic spacecraft has a large dish antenna, exposed instrument booms, and a compact central bus.
A small robotic Moon vehicle has chunky metal wheels, a low instrument body, cameras, and solar panels.
An open Moon buggy has wire-mesh wheels, two simple seats, a dish antenna, and exposed equipment racks.
An uncrewed cylindrical orbital supply craft has a docking nose, rounded cargo body, and paired solar arrays.
A small central spacecraft stretches a vast thin reflective sail across long lightweight booms.
A squat instrument capsule sits within a broad saucer-shaped heat shield and protective rear shell.
A small futuristic combat craft has a pointed cockpit, compact wings, engine nozzles, and weapon mounts.
A bulky working spacecraft has exposed cargo containers, docking structures, and large rear engine clusters.
A vast elongated spacecraft carries rotating habitat drums, agricultural decks, and a distant propulsion section.
A smooth circular disc has a raised central dome, shallow rim, and lights or landing legs underneath.
A huge armored spacecraft has heavy gun turrets, layered hull plating, and a massive bank of engines.
A vast spacecraft has open hangar bays, a broad launch deck, and clusters of small fighter craft nearby.
A large circular inhabited ring connects by spokes to a central docking hub.
A large long-range craft has clustered passenger modules and detachable surface-landing pods.
An organic-looking spacecraft has ribbed surfaces, curved appendages, and a shell-like hull.
A globular spacecraft has circular viewports, small landing legs, and thrusters arranged around its hull.
A rugged industrial spacecraft has a forward drilling assembly, articulated grabber arms, and ore bins.
